author: Nayan Seth
description:
US President Donald Trump’s claim on Tuesday that Washington would catch up to China on rare earth supplies “within 10 months” is “unrealistic” and “diplomatic bluster”, given Beijing’s decades-long dominance in supply chains, experts say.
“The US will not catch up with China in rare earths production, processing or end-user rare earth-enabled product manufacturing in the next 10 months or the next 10 years,” said Jack Lifton, co-chairman of the Critical Minerals Institute, a global think...
title: Trump claims US will have enough rare earths in 10 months; experts call it unrealistic

author: Seong Hyeon Choi
description:
Acting US Navy Secretary Hung Cao told senators on Tuesday that shipbuilders from allies such as South Korea and Japan could help the United States rebuild its shipyards and narrow China’s lead, as lawmakers pressed him to keep warship construction on American soil.
Cao made his remarks in an opening statement at a Senate Committee on Armed Services hearing to confirm his nomination to become the new Secretary of the Navy.
The Navy veteran of three decades said the US is in an era of...
title: US Navy chief urges US lawmakers to strengthen shipbuilding capacity to close gap on China

author: Alex Lo
description:
She might not be a spy after all, but she could have been. That, apparently, is US intelligence’s current assessment of Alice Huang, the microchip siren blamed for bringing down AI titan Jensen Huang.
“The US intelligence community is still working to understand the relationship between a Chinese businesswoman who had an affair with [then] Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and the Chinese government,” CNN reported, citing multiple sources.
“The intelligence collected on her to date,” it said, “does not...
title: Spy or not, Alice Huang was a useful pawn

author: Igor Patrick
description:
Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva came up with the idea for the meeting between US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said on Monday, days before the three leaders were due to meet in Shenzhen.
“He told me yesterday that he had encouraged this meeting to help bring about an end to the war in Ukraine,” Carney told reporters on the sidelines of the Francophonie summit in Phnom Penh.
Carney, who...
title: Shenzhen summit of Xi, Trump and Putin was Brazil’s Lula’s idea, Carney claims

author: Lucy Quaggin
description:
Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has agreed to testify before the US Congress amid scrutiny over national security risks following revelations that he had an extramarital affair with a businesswoman suspected of working for Chinese intelligence.
On December 1, Huang will voluntarily appear for transcribed interviews before the Select Committee on China, the House Foreign Affairs Committee and the House Intelligence Committee. Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter will testify before the committees on...
title: Jensen Huang agrees to face Congress over Nvidia scandal

author: Khushboo Razdan
description:
Barely hours after arriving in Manila on Tuesday, US President Donald Trump was already looking ahead to his meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen. “We have some very important things to discuss,” he said.
Trump also appeared to be anticipating the reception awaiting him in the southern Chinese tech hub. “I hear we’re going to have quite a landing. It’s going to be a beautiful thing,” he said.
First up, however, was a series of engagements around the Association of Southeast...
title: Trump eyes China after brief Manila stop, seeking chemistry with Xi amid fresh AI strains

author: Orange Wang
description:
US President Donald Trump’s suggestion on Monday that he might meet North Korean leader Kim Jong-un in China this week has thrown up a logistical challenge.
According to the White House’s schedule, Trump is due to arrive in Shenzhen on Wednesday evening for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit and return to the United States on Thursday, with no other Chinese stops listed.
Meanwhile, Kim was visiting Samjiyon near North Korea’s border with China on Sunday and Monday, according to...
title: Planes, trains and automobiles: what we know about Kim Jong-un’s foreign travels

author: Dewey Sim
description:
US President Donald Trump arrived in Manila on Tuesday to start a three-day Asian swing, seeking to deepen ties with the region just weeks after his Republican Party suffered heavy losses in the midterm elections.
In the Philippine capital for the annual gathering of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean), Trump held talks with leaders of the Quad – the informal grouping of the United States, Australia, India and Japan – before joining a meeting with Southeast Asian leaders.
Trump...
title: A trade deal, rare earths and a Quad revival: day 1 of Trump’s Asia trip

author: Carol Yang
description:
In Beijing’s diplomatic protocols, choreography can carry the same weight as a communique.
When Chinese President Xi Jinping takes his place at the end of the red carpet to welcome visitors to the Apec summit on Thursday, many eyes will be on his brief encounter with Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi.
It will be her first trip to China since taking office in October last year, but relations have been in the deep freeze for the past 12 months after Takaichi said a Taiwan Strait crisis could...
title: A handshake but no smile, is this the best that Takaichi can hope for in China?

author: Amber Wang
description:
The delegation with the US president on his trip to Asia includes an inner circle of diplomatic, economic and trade officials as well as Donald Trump’s newly appointed White House chief of staff.
Among the 17 people travelling with Trump on Air Force One on Tuesday were Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Trade Representative Jamieson Greer and chief of staff Stephen Miller.
Notably absent from the White House travel list is...
title: Who was with Trump on Air Force One for the trip to Asia?

author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
The Chinese air force appears to have significantly expanded one of its largest annual combat exercises, with satellite imagery showing nearly 300 aircraft across 11 bases in western China.
The scale of the manoeuvres suggests China may be testing its ability to bring together hundreds of aircraft for prolonged operations, while developing the coordination and logistical support needed to sustain a major air campaign, according to analysts.
The build-up, which compares with 194 visible aircraft...
title: What does China’s massive warplane build-up say about its combat readiness?

author: Ling Xin
description:
China has carried out its first large-scale trial of seabed ore mining in international waters, using a robotic vehicle to gather potato-sized, metal-rich rocks from the eastern Pacific between Hawaii and Mexico, according to state media.
The rocks collected during the trial – known as polymetallic nodules – contain nickel, cobalt, manganese and copper, which are key ingredients in the batteries used for electric cars and smartphones.
To support the survey work, China deployed a one-of-a-kind...
title: China taps Pacific metals trove in first large-scale seabed ore mining trial

author: Lawrence Chung
description:
Taiwan’s military said it closely monitored two Russian warplanes flying near the island on Tuesday, the same day that Moscow’s military aviation activity prompted fighter jet scrambles in Japan and South Korea.
The aircraft were detected early in the day approaching from the northeast before flying along the island’s eastern coast and departing to the southeast of Taitung county, according to the Taiwanese defence ministry.
“The armed forces used joint intelligence, surveillance and...
title: Taiwan tracks 2 Russian warplanes off eastern coast ahead of Apec summit

author: Cao Jiaxuan
description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney have agreed on broader trade concessions as Ottawa seeks to reset relations with Beijing amid growing trade tensions with the United States.
The two leaders met ahead of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation leaders’ meeting in Shenzhen on Tuesday, where they discussed ways of managing their differences.
Xi, who was meeting the Canadian leader for the second time this year, called for greater “political trust through...
title: China and Canada agree on fresh tariff relief as Xi and Carney continue thaw

author: Carol Yang
description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping has pledged to deepen connectivity between China and Vietnam and better integrate their shared interests in a meeting with his Vietnamese counterpart To Lam.
President Lam arrived in Shenzhen earlier on Tuesday for the Apec summit. Vietnam will host next year’s gathering.
Calling for stronger mutual trust, unity and all-round cooperation, Xi said the two countries should expand their connectivity, align their interests and promote development.
“As comrades and...
title: China and Vietnam should ‘weather the storm together’, Xi tells Lam in Shenzhen

author: Alcott Wei
description:
China has charged a former senior nuclear industry executive with bribery, marking the latest downfall in its sweeping anti-corruption crackdown targeting the military and defence sectors.
Gu Jun, former general manager of state-owned giant China National Nuclear Corporation (CNNC), will stand trial for accepting illegal payments, the Supreme People’s Procuratorate in Beijing announced on Tuesday.
Gu is accused of long abusing his position in the nuclear power sector to secure favours for...
title: China charges veteran nuclear expert Gu Jun with taking ‘huge’ bribes

author: SCMP Reporters
description:
This live article is freely available to our registered users. Please log in or create an account.
The United States president’s Air Force One is on the ground in Manila where President Donald Trump will speak at the Asean summit.
He has just over 20 hours for a state visit that Manila pushed hard to secure.
Manila adjusted the summit calendar to accommodate Trump’s preference for a short layover en route to the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, where a Xi-Trump-Putin trilateral has been...
title: Donald Trump arrives in Manila to speak at Asean summit before heading to China

author: Brian Rhoads,Raymond Ma
description:
President Xi Jinping will discuss “world peace” with Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin on Thursday in the first-ever trilateral meeting between the leaders of China, the US and Russia.
The talks “will be of groundbreaking significance”, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson said on Monday. The meeting, alongside the Apec summit in Shenzhen, will start at 2.30pm following a 12.45pm Trump-Xi discussion, according to the White House.
What exactly the leaders will talk about is unclear, with China...
title: Xi-Trump-Putin meeting’s symbolism to far outweigh concrete results

author: William Zheng
description:
Tightening Communist Party discipline is vital for stability and development, Beijing’s top foreign ministry envoy in Hong Kong said as he briefed the city’s diplomatic community on the outcomes of the party’s latest plenum.
Cui Jianchun, the head of the Office of the Commissioner of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Hong Kong, outlined the main takeaways of the fifth plenum, held in Beijing last month.
The gathering resulted in the adoption of a landmark resolution on strengthening party...
title: Ahead of Apec, Beijing’s Hong Kong envoy says party discipline removes ‘serious dangers’

author: Albee Zhang
description:
The first two American F-15EX Eagle II fighter jets arrived at Kadena in Okinawa, Japan on Sunday marking an upgrade for the ageing US fleet, but analysts say a shift in the regional air power balance is unlikely given China’s growing capabilities.
Kadena is the first airbase to receive the F-15EX outside the United States, according to a US Air Force statement on Saturday. The new aircraft will be operated by the 44th and 67th Fighter Squadrons under the 18th Wing.
They are the first of 36...
title: US airbase Kadena gets F-15EX fighters but no upper hand against China, analysts say

author: Victoria Bela
description:
Chinese scientists have harnessed the process of water evaporation to generate continuous electricity day and night using a unique device made from lotus plants, according to a paper published in the peer-reviewed journal Device.
The hydrovoltaic technology could provide low-maintenance power for distributed sensors and low-power electronics in off-grid locations next to large water bodies, said the paper, which appeared on November 2.
The team’s lotus-stem and bacteria generator achieved...
title: China team produces endless energy from lotus stems with water evaporation power

author: Han Li
description:
US prosecutors spent about six hours on Monday delivering their closing arguments in the criminal trial of Huawei Technologies at a packed federal court in New York. The case – one of the most high-profile legal battles involving a Chinese technology giant – has dragged on for almost eight years.
Huawei and three affiliated companies face 12 remaining criminal counts, including racketeering conspiracy, which prosecutors allege involved the companies reinvesting profits from a pattern of criminal...
title: US prosecutors make final case against Huawei in theft, fraud trial

author: Jianlu Bi
description:
As leaders from across the Asia-Pacific converge on Shenzhen this week for the annual Apec Economic Leaders’ Meeting, global attention has zeroed in on a planned, unprecedented sideline gathering: a trilateral summit bringing together President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump.
At a moment when the international order is strained by protracted regional wars, supply chain fragmentation and eroding strategic trust, any direct engagement among Beijing,...
title: Xi-Putin-Trump meeting in Shenzhen is no Yalta 2.0

author: Chao Kong
description:
A newly released photograph in a US intelligence report has offered a rare glimpse of what is widely believed to be China’s secret Shenlong spaceplane in orbit, showing its payload bay doors open.
In the image released by the US Defence Intelligence Agency (DIA) on October 26, a lone spacecraft is visible. Neither the DIA nor Beijing has said whether it is a Shenlong spaceplane.
The photo raises a question: how many reusable orbital vehicles like Shenlong would be needed for a rapid global...
title: 40 Chinese spaceplanes could hit any target on Earth in minutes: study
